What is DeepL?

Neural machine translation service widely regarded as producing the most natural-sounding output, particularly between European languages. Now extended with DeepL Write (a monolingual style and grammar editor) and DeepL Voice for live meeting translation.

Best for

High-quality document translation between well-supported European languages with terminology control.

Main features

  • Document translation preserving formatting (DOCX, PPTX, PDF, XLSX, HTML)
  • glossaries enforcing terminology
  • formal/informal tone control
  • DeepL Write for rephrasing and style
  • DeepL Voice for real-time meeting and conversation translation
  • Clarify for ambiguous-source questions
  • desktop apps with a global hotkey
  • browser extensions.

Practical use cases

  • Translating contracts and technical documentation while keeping layout
  • enforcing approved terminology across a company
  • polishing English written by a non-native speaker
  • live translation in Teams meetings
  • translating a website.

Who is it for?

  • Professional translators, legal and technical writers, international businesses, localisation teams, and anyone drafting in a second language.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium; per-seat subscription; separate character-metered API

Plans described in the source

Free with strict limits. Starter around $8.74/user/mo billed annually. Advanced around $28.99/user/mo annually. Ultimate around $57.49/user/mo annually. DeepL API Free allows 500,000 characters/month at no cost; DeepL API Pro is roughly $5.49/mo plus about $25 per million characters. Prices vary by region and currency (EUR pricing differs from USD).

Free plan

Yes - free web and app translation with character and document limits, plus a free API tier of 500,000 characters/month.

Free trial

Yes - 30-day free trial typically offered on Pro plans.

Usage limits to consider

Free web tier caps text at ~1,500-5,000 characters per translation and 3 document translations per month with size limits and no editing of the output file. Paid tiers raise or remove document counts by tier. API Free is hard-capped at 500,000 characters/month.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Consistently rated the most natural translation output in its strongest language pairs
  • glossaries give genuine terminology control
  • document translation preserves complex formatting well
  • strong GDPR posture with EU data processing and no training on Pro data
  • clean, well-documented API.

Limitations to consider

  • Language coverage is far narrower than Google Translate
  • Arabic and non-European languages are noticeably weaker than French/German/Spanish
  • free tier limits are restrictive
  • per-seat pricing adds up for large teams
  • DeepL Voice availability is limited by platform and language.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Chrome/Edge/Firefox extensions, Word and Outlook add-ins

Languages

  • 30+ languages including Arabic (added later than others), French, English, and all major European languages; quality is notably highest between European pairs

API access

Yes - DeepL API with free and Pro tiers, character-metered; well-documented REST API with official SDKs

Integrations and exports

  • Microsoft Word, Outlook, Teams, Google Workspace, Chrome, Trados, memoQ, Zendesk, Salesforce, Confluence, Jira, Slack

Evaluation notes

For Arabic work, test against Google Translate and Microsoft Translator before standardising - DeepL's advantage is much smaller outside European pairs. The API Free tier at 500K characters/month is genuinely useful for prototyping.
